title: Content From Major Assignment 2
description: Major Project II was a front-end development project that involved incorporating video-based content into a webpage design. I produced a website that showcases different drum beats alongside their associated notation, with the goal of creating an educational resource for learning and reference.

title: Preserv
description: Preserv is a senior design capstone project created in collaboration with four other team members. I was tasked with managing the overall production of the high-fidelity prototype, ensuring consistency across different screens, interactions, and user flows, and helping shape the final product into a cohesive and functional user experience.

title: Recipe Notebook
description: Recipe Notebook was a semester-long user-centered design project focused on developing an application and iteratively improving its functionality through user testing and market analysis. The project emphasized validating design decisions with real user feedback and evidence-based iteration.

title: Comic Strip
description: Created for a class focused on advanced photo editing techniques, this project involved designing a comic strip using open-source, freely available images sourced from the web, combined with original digital drawing and painting. The final work emphasizes image composition, layering, and visual storytelling.

title: Native Quiz App
description: This mobile quiz application was developed as part of a mobile development course while I was learning the fundamentals of React. The app uses stack navigation to manage multiple screens within a single application. It features a themed trivia game centered around Spider-Man, complete with interactive questions and built-in game logic to track user progress and calculate scores in real time. Through this project, I gained hands-on experience with component-based architecture, navigation patterns, and state management in a mobile environment.

title: Native Exercise App
description: This exercise-focused mobile application was developed using React Native, building on an earlier version originally created in standard React for the web. The project served as a practical exploration of how core React concepts translate into a native mobile environment. It leverages hooks such as useState and useEffect to manage timers and repetition counters, demonstrating how familiar logic can be adapted to work with native components. Through this project, I strengthened my understanding of both frameworks and gained experience bridging the gap between web-based React and mobile app development.

title: Toon-Tier
description: Toon Tier is a full-stack web application built with React for the frontend and Supabase for the backend, designed as a cartoon rating and tracking platform. Users can create accounts, manage watchlists (watching, completed, dropped), and leave ratings and reviews that are visible across the site. If I were to continue developing Toon Tier, I would expand its community features by adding a friend system to allow users to connect and view each other’s activity, as well as an online forum/discussion section to encourage deeper engagement. I would also revisit parts of the UI/UX to improve consistency and scalability as the platform grows.

title: Cafe-Lunar
description: Cafe Lunar is a mock business website designed and developed as a rapid-turnaround project using Claude Code for AI-assisted development. Built in approximately 3 hours, it was created using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript to simulate a real-world landing page for a café brand. If I were to revisit Cafe Lunar, I would potentially convert it into a component-based framework for easier scalability and reuse.
